accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE statutory RSHE guidance (2019), primary Health and prevention ('the facts and science relating to allergies') and Basic first aid ('how to make a clear and efficient call to emergency services'); the NHS Food allergy page for the signs (itchy mouth, raised itchy rash/hives, swelling of face, lips, tongue or around the eyes, tummy pain, being sick; anaphylaxis: breathing difficulty, wheeze, cough, feeling faint, treated with adrenaline and a 999 call); the Food Standards Agency list of 14 allergens that UK labels must show; and Perry et al. (2004, J Allergy Clin Immunol 113:973-976) for hand cleaning: liquid soap, bar soap or wipes removed peanut allergen, hand sanitiser often left it. Cheese being made from milk and nut-picking leaving traces are standard allergy-charity advice (Anaphylaxis UK, Allergy UK).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the adult text: same food safe for everyone (predict 1 and the looking glass showing Sam allergic and Leo allergic to milk instead; p1, challenge 'same'), no badge means safe to share (predict 2, p3, challenge 'badge'), sharing or swapping (Swap, Give a bite and Share crisps refused in Do, 'share'), gel cleans food bits (predict 3, gel rub leaves all 14 bits, p5, 'gel'), wiping on trousers ('legs'), pressing a friend ('press'), picking nuts out ('pick', m1), hidden milk in cheese ('hidden', m3), keeping quiet ('secret', m8), calling it fussy ('fussy', m6) and waiting to see (predict 4, 'wait', m2).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagallergy is built on this topic's own mechanisms: a draggable looking glass that reveals how one food acts in three different bodies, a Do / Don't lunch sort, a hand-scrubbing simulation where rubbing with soap removes peanut bits one by one while gel leaves them and trousers move them, a reply picker whose kind answer moves position each round, and a sign-spotting grid gated before the tell-a-grown-up choice. 1046 Fire safety (flaggetout) and 211 Rules that keep us safe cover different hazards; no other lab models allergen transfer. Lab shingle similarity is under 30% against every flag_*.js (lab_distinct gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each rule before it is stated: peanuts are fine for Ava and Leo but not Sam (and Leo's milk allergy appears), unsafe lunch cards bounce out of Do with the reason, rubbing with gel leaves '14 bits left' and a 'shiny, but the bits are still there' label while soap counts down to 0, trousers show 'on trousers: n', a pressing reply is refused with 'even a tiny bit can make someone very ill', a yawn is refused as a sign, and the action choice appears only after the four real signs are found. Done messages confirm only after the action.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Yes, for everyone' (the looking glass shows Sam allergic), 'Yes, no badge means safe' (sharing cards are refused and the reason says allergies are not always on a badge), 'Yes, gel cleans everything' (gel rubbing removes no bits) and 'Wait and see' (choosing wait is refused: signs can get worse fast).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions whose wrong options carry eleven distinct slip messages: same, share, badge, gel, legs, press, pick, hidden, secret, fussy and wait, each naming the exact mistake (for example 'Cheese is made from milk! Milk hides in lots of foods' and 'Gel kills germs, but the peanut bits stay on. Use soap and water').

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short paragraphs at FK grade 1.7 (limit 5.0) with everyday words (body, lunch, share, soap, grown-up); lab cards are two to six words with emoji for a 6 to 7 year old. Adult text is FK 8.9 (limit 10.0) and keeps the precise terms (immune system, food protein, allergen, hives, anaphylaxis, adrenaline auto-injector).

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one rule with its reason (bodies differ, eat your own lunch, wash with soap, stop asking, tell a grown-up); adult paragraphs give the statutory basis and what an allergy is, the NHS signs and the child's role, the named mistakes with a do-not-frighten caution, and what the lab does. No content-gate filler phrase matches.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every step: three friend circles with name and result tags and a full-width result note; two Do / Don't bins whose sorted cards become wrapped mini cards (fixed after the long 'Ask a grown-up if offered food' line clipped); the hands panel with 14 bits and three tool tiles with wrapped labels (fixed after 'Wipe on my trousers' clipped); three full-width reply rows; the six signs in a 2 by 3 grid of tiles with wrapped labels (redesigned after scattered circles overlapped) and three action tiles. walk.cjs passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Look at Ava / Sam / Leo, Pick <card> then Put it in Do / Don't, Soap and water / Hand gel / Wipe on my trousers plus Rub hands, the three replies, each sign and each action. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each scene description and each piece of feedback, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, right and wrong tiles carry ✓ / ✗ or ⚠ text as well as colour, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found nothing in light or dark on desktop and phone.
